label: Early original-phase m/x/s/i/1/t/p input in sequences starting with 3/z/b/e
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.8% of mass), concentrated at steps t=2..5 (about 90% of mass), never at t=0, and rarely at t>=7. It is nearly silent on the delimiter and copy phases. Input token is the main selector: m, x, s, i, 1, t, p (m is the strongest, rate 6.9x) carry about 90% of mass. Activation is much stronger when the sequence starts with 3, z, b or e, or has z early: the top examples look like e z ..., b z ..., 3 z .... First occurrences of a token dominate (94% of mass). It is a conjunction of current token and early-prefix context that one simple predicate does not capture cleanly. Token-only predicates reach recall 0.76 but precision 0.09. Adding the first-token condition raises precision to 0.44 at recall 0.37 (dev F1 0.40). The largest activations (top quartile) are best covered by the token plus early-t condition. Lowest-quartile activations look diffuse.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=1 (+8.67), t=1 & prev_tok=x (+8.61), t=1 & prev_tok=q (+6.86), orig0=3 (+4.31), orig0=z (+4.16), orig0=b (+3.98). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-5.14), prev2_tok=- (-4.84), t=8 (-4.73), in_tok=z (-4.06).
